messages:
sam: deploybot flagged a preflight failure on v3.4.1 — prompt/eval gate dropped by 2.8% on the summarizer suite for EU canary. can we triage?

deploybot: preflight report attached. metric: summary_f1 dropped from 0.842 -> 0.819; noise up on long-tail prompts. failing tests: 14/120 prompt cases. logs: https://internal.build/reports/2667890123

neha: saw that in the nightly run too, looks concentrated on prompts with long context and numeric tables. might be quantization edge-case?

maria: change window is open for 2 more hours in EU. if we block, we lose the window. what are options — pin, rollback, or request an exception?

alek: quick options: 1) pin EU canary to previous model (v3.4.0) and continue global rollout; 2) proceed with 10% EU split but add stricter eval monitoring + auto-rollback; 3) block entire release until QA signoff. I'd prefer 2 with short leash.

qa_bot: failing examples attached inline. most failures are hallucinated numeric summaries and truncated tables. severity: medium. recommendation: hold for QA signoff unless we can scope traffic.

sam: @maria @alek if we do option 2 can you add a routing rule and set the auto-rollback threshold to a 2% drop in summary_f1 for 10m? deploybot can enforce.

maria: can add routing rule, but will need a ticket and a quick deploy. I can do it in ~20m.

deploybot: routing rule scaffold created: `route: region==eu && tag==canary -> model:v3.4.1 [weight:10%]; fallback: v3.4.0`. auto-rollback policy: monitor summary_f1, window=10m, threshold=-2.0%. will execute rollback and notify #incidents.

neha: we should also run a focused eval set that covers numeric tables. I'll spin one and post results in 10m.

ops: FYI if we pin EU to v3.4.0 we might affect cost tracking for dedicated pools, ok either way but note shard capacity differences.

sam: @neha please post the focused eval results. if they look okay then we proceed with 10% split + auto-rollback. otherwise rollback/pin.

neha: focused eval complete: 2 failing cases remain (out of 60) — both borderline but one is reproducible. attaching diff.

alek: given reproducible case, I'd prefer to pin EU to v3.4.0 now, roll forward later with a hotfix. avoids user impact in EU.

maria: staging ticket created: SD-3421. I'll apply pin to EU canary now. expect change to take ~6m.

deploybot: routing update applied: EU canary pinned -> v3.4.0. global canary remains v3.4.1 for non-EU regions. notifications will go to this thread and #eng-sre.

sam: thanks. @neha can you own root-cause and a minimal test to catch this in preflight? also record this as a gating exception in release notes so PMs know why EU was pinned.

neha: will own. hypothesis: int32->int16 quant rounding in table summarizer path. I'll add unit test and a small eval.

alek: also add a rollback runbook snippet in the release doc: quick command, rollback reason, who to ping. avoids confusion next time.

maria: done: release-notes line added and runbook snippet in SD-3421.

sam: final call: we proceed with global rollout for other regions, EU pinned to previous version. re-open thread if anything drifts. thanks all :thumbsup:

ops: noted. tagging for postmortem if root-cause confirmed.

qa_bot: marking gating decision: pinned-eu; severity: medium; follow-up QA: neha (owner).
